articles.title: The Wallet on the Bus
articles.text:
On Tuesday evening I found a brown wallet under the seat on the number twelve bus.

My first thought was to [[ignore]] it. The bus was crowded, I was already late, and somebody else would surely pick it up. Then I thought about the face of the person who had lost it, and I could not [[accept]] that excuse.

I asked the driver what to do. He told me to [[report]] it at the station office, and he wanted me to [[describe]] exactly where the wallet had been.

The clerk at the office was patient. She asked me to [[complete]] a short form — where, when, and what the wallet looked like — and then to [[print]] my name clearly at the bottom.

Inside there were two bank cards, a student card and nine hundred dollars. The clerk did not [[blame]] me for opening it; she said anyone would have done the same.

"Most people just [[avoid]] this kind of trouble," she said. "It takes twenty minutes and you get nothing for it."

I told her I did not [[expect]] anything. I only wanted the owner to [[receive]] it back.

Three days later my phone rang. A university student had come to [[search]] for the wallet barely an hour after I handed it in. She wanted to [[offer]] me a reward, and I had to [[refuse]] three times before she finally believed me.

Then she said something I still [[remind]] myself of. She had almost stopped believing strangers, and one small thing had changed her mind for a whole year.

I did nothing clever that day. I did not [[solve]] a crime or save a life. I simply did not walk away.

articles.title: Two Months Before the Science Fair
articles.text:
Our group of four had two months to [[produce]] something for the science fair, and for three weeks we did almost nothing at all.

We could not agree on a topic. Wei wanted to [[invent]] a machine. Ting wanted to [[compare]] the water in four different rivers. We would [[argue]] about it for an hour after school and then go home.

Our teacher finally made us [[divide]] the work between us. "Stop trying to [[create]] one perfect idea," she said. "Choose the smaller one, and then [[improve]] it a little every week."

We chose the rivers. Every Saturday we went out to [[gather]] samples in small glass bottles, and Ting made me [[arrange]] them by date before we went home. Wei built a rough filter to [[detect]] the dirt we could not see with our eyes.

Slowly the project began to [[develop]] a shape of its own. The numbers from week one did not [[match]] the numbers from week four, and that difference turned into the whole story: the water below the factory got worse after every heavy rain.

On the evening before the fair our poster was still half empty. We stayed in the classroom until nine, and nobody had to [[suggest]] staying — we all simply did.

At the fair the judges asked us to [[discuss]] what had surprised us most. Wei answered first, and for once he did not talk too much.

We did not win. We came fourth. But all four of us agreed to [[continue]] the study next year, with better bottles and an earlier start.

articles.title: The Night the Lights Went Out
articles.text:
The radio began to [[broadcast]] the typhoon warning at six in the morning.

By eight the school had decided to [[cancel]] every class. My mother did not [[waste]] a single minute. She sent my brother out to [[lock]] the back gate and told me to [[shut]] every window on the second floor.

"Tape the glass," she said. "It will not stop a typhoon, but it may [[protect]] you from the pieces."

My father came home at ten with rice, eggs and a box of candles. Shops cannot [[provide]] anything once the wind really starts, he said, and we must not [[depend]] on the power staying on.

By midnight the wind had begun to [[shake]] the metal door at the back of the house. At two the lights went out.

My grandmother sat by the window and did not look worried at all. She told us how her village had to [[survive]] three days without any help in 1959, and how neighbours would [[support]] one another with whatever food was left.

Her voice did [[calm]] my little sister, who had been crying since the room went dark. My mother would [[insist]] that we eat properly even by candlelight, so we had rice and eggs at a table we could barely see.

By morning the wind had dropped. Branches, roof tiles and one entire bicycle lay across our street. Neighbours came out early to [[lift]] the heavy branches off the road, and nobody waited to be asked.

It took two more days for the water to [[return]] to the taps. I did not [[realize]] until then how much an ordinary quiet morning is worth.

grammar.title: 現在簡單式：第三人稱單數
grammar.sub: He / She / It 的動詞要加 -s
grammar.point: 講「平常、習慣、每天都這樣」的事，用現在簡單式。主詞如果是 he、she、it 或一個人、一個東西，動詞要加 -s 或 -es；其他主詞（I、you、we、they）動詞維持原形。
grammar.tips: go、do、watch 這種以 o、ch、sh、s、x 結尾的字加 -es：goes、does、watches。
examples: She goes to school by bus.
她搭公車上學。
My father watches the news every night.
我爸爸每天晚上看新聞。
They live in Taipei.
他們住在台北。（主詞是 they，動詞不加 s）

questions.stem: My sister ___ the piano every evening.
questions.why: 主詞 My sister 是第三人稱單數，動詞要加 -s。
主詞 My brother 是單數，go 要變成 goes。

questions.answer: He gets up at six every morning
questions.why: 主詞 He 用 gets；時間放句尾。

grammar.title: 現在進行式
grammar.sub: be 動詞 + V-ing：現在正在做
grammar.point: 講「此刻正在發生」的事，用 be 動詞（am / is / are）加上動詞的 -ing 形式。主詞是 I 用 am，he/she/it 用 is，you/we/they 用 are。
grammar.tips: 常跟 now、right now、at the moment、Look! 一起出現。
examples: I am doing my homework now.
我現在正在寫功課。
Look! The baby is sleeping.
你看！寶寶正在睡覺。
They are waiting for the bus.
他們正在等公車。

questions.stem: Be quiet! The baby ___ .
questions.why: 「現在正在睡」用現在進行式 is + sleeping。
be 動詞後面要用 V-ing，watch 要變 watching。

questions.zh: 我媽媽正在廚房煮晚餐。
questions.answer: My mother is cooking dinner in the kitchen
questions.why: is + cooking 表示正在進行，地點放句尾。

grammar.title: 過去簡單式
grammar.point: 講已經發生、結束的事，動詞要用過去式。規則變化加 -ed（walk → walked）；不規則的要背（go → went、eat → ate、buy → bought）。否定與疑問用 did，後面動詞回到原形。
grammar.tips: 看到 yesterday、last night、two days ago、in 2020 幾乎都是過去式。
examples: We visited my grandmother last Sunday.
我們上週日去看了我奶奶。
He went to Japan two years ago.
他兩年前去了日本。
I did not finish my homework last night.
我昨晚沒有寫完功課。

questions.stem: We ___ a new bike for my brother last week.
questions.why: last week 是過去，buy 的過去式是 bought。
didn't 後面的動詞要用原形，所以是 didn't go。

questions.zh: 他昨天在公園遇到他的老師。
questions.answer: He met his teacher in the park yesterday
questions.why: meet 的過去式是 met；地點在前、時間在後。

grammar.title: 形容詞比較級
grammar.point: 兩個東西比較時，短的形容詞加 -er（tall → taller），長的形容詞（三個音節以上、或 -ful、-ous 結尾）前面加 more（more beautiful）。比較的對象前面要加 than。
grammar.tips: good → better、bad → worse、many/much → more 是不規則的，要背。
examples: My brother is taller than me.
我哥哥比我高。
This question is more difficult than that one.
這一題比那一題難。
Today is better than yesterday.
今天比昨天好。

questions.stem: This box is ___ than that one, so I will carry it.
questions.why: 兩者比較用比較級；heavy 去 y 加 -ier 變 heavier。
比較的對象前面要用 than，不是 that。

questions.zh: 這部電影比那本書有趣。
questions.answer: This movie is more interesting than that book
questions.why: interesting 是長形容詞，用 more + 原級 + than。

grammar.title: 未來式
grammar.point: will 用在「現在才決定、單純的預測」；be going to 用在「已經打算好、或有跡象快發生」。兩者後面都接動詞原形。
grammar.tips: It is going to rain.（天很黑了，快下雨）／I will help you.（現在才決定要幫忙）
examples: I will call you tonight.
我今晚會打給你。
We are going to visit Tainan next month.
我們下個月要去台南。
Look at the sky. It is going to rain.
看看天空，快下雨了。

questions.stem: Look at those dark clouds. It ___ rain soon.
questions.why: 已經有跡象（烏雲）表示快發生，用 be going to。
will 後面直接接動詞原形，不加 to。

questions.zh: 我們下個週末要去海邊。
questions.answer: We are going to the beach next weekend
questions.why: be going to + 地點，表示已經計畫好的行程。

grammar.title: There is / There are
grammar.point: 表示「有」某個東西存在時，用 There is（後接單數或不可數名詞）或 There are（後接複數名詞）。動詞要跟著後面那個名詞變，不是跟 there 變。
grammar.tips: 否定是 There is not / There are not；疑問把 be 動詞提前：Is there…? Are there…?
examples: There is a cat under the table.
桌子底下有一隻貓。
There are twenty students in my class.
我班上有二十個學生。
Is there any milk in the fridge?
冰箱裡還有牛奶嗎？

questions.stem: ___ three books and a pen on the desk.
questions.why: 後面是複數（three books），所以用 There are。
many people 是複數，要用 There are。

questions.zh: 我家附近有一間便利商店。
questions.answer: There is a convenience store near my house
questions.why: 單數名詞用 There is，地點放句尾。

phrases.note: look for 是「找」的動作（還沒找到）；find 是「找到」的結果。
examples: I am looking for my keys.
我正在找我的鑰匙。
She looked for a new job all summer.
她整個夏天都在找新工作。

questions.stem: 尋找
questions.why: look for＝尋找；look after＝照顧；look at＝看著。

questions.stem: What are you ___ ? Maybe I can help you find it.
questions.why: 後面說「幫你找到」，所以前面是正在尋找。

questions.zh: 他在書桌底下找他的手機。
questions.answer: He is looking for his phone under the desk
questions.why: look for + 要找的東西。

examples: Could you look after my dog this weekend?
這個週末你可以幫我照顧狗嗎？
She looks after her little brother after school.
她放學後照顧她弟弟。

questions.stem: 照顧
questions.why: look after＝照顧，跟 take care of 同義。

questions.stem: My aunt will ___ the baby while my mother is at work.
questions.why: 照顧小孩用 look after。
look after 後面直接接受詞，不要多一個 to。

phrases.note: 除了照顧人，也可以指「處理」一件事。
examples: I will take care of the dishes tonight.
今晚碗我來洗。
Who takes care of your cat when you travel?
你旅行時誰照顧你的貓？

questions.stem: 照料；處理
questions.why: take care of＝照料、處理。

questions.stem: Do not worry about the tickets. I will ___ them.
questions.why: 這裡是「我會處理」。

questions.answer: She takes care of her grandmother at home
questions.why: 主詞是 She，take 要加 -s。

phrases.note: get up 是「起床、起身」；wake up 是「醒來」。可以 wake up 之後躺著不 get up。
examples: I get up at six every morning.
我每天早上六點起床。
He got up late and missed the bus.
他太晚起床，錯過了公車。

questions.stem: 起床
questions.why: get up＝起床；give up＝放棄；grow up＝長大。

questions.stem: She ___ at five to catch the first train.
questions.why: 為了趕第一班車而早起。
yesterday 前面不加 in，直接說 yesterday。

phrases.note: 相反是 turn off。開電視、燈、電腦用 turn on，不用 open。
examples: Please turn on the light; it is too dark.
請開燈，太暗了。
He turned on the radio and started to cook.
他打開收音機開始煮飯。

questions.stem: 打開（電器）
questions.why: turn on＝打開電器；turn off＝關掉。

questions.stem: It is dark in here. Could you ___ the light?
questions.why: 太暗了所以要開燈。
電器用 turn on，不用 open。

phrases.note: 離開房間前關燈、關冷氣都用 turn off。
examples: Remember to turn off the air conditioner.
記得關冷氣。
She turned off her phone during the exam.
考試時她把手機關機。

questions.stem: 關掉（電器）
questions.why: turn off＝關掉電器。

questions.stem: Please ___ the lights when you leave the classroom.
questions.why: 離開教室要關燈。

questions.answer: He turned off the TV before he went to bed
questions.why: turn off 的過去式是 turned off。

phrases.note: at 後面接名詞或動名詞（V-ing），不是動詞原形。
examples: She is good at math.
她擅長數學。
My brother is good at playing basketball.
我哥哥很會打籃球。

questions.stem: 擅長
questions.why: be good at＝擅長。

questions.stem: He is good at ___ pictures of animals.
questions.why: at 是介系詞，後面要用動名詞 V-ing。

questions.answer: My sister is good at speaking English
questions.why: be good at + V-ing。

phrases.note: 等「人或東西」要加 for；不能說 wait somebody。
examples: We waited for the bus for half an hour.
我們等公車等了半小時。
Do not wait for me; start without me.
不用等我，你們先開始。

questions.stem: 等待
questions.why: wait for＝等待。

questions.stem: A lot of people are ___ the train on the platform.
questions.why: 等某個東西要用 wait for。
wait 後面要加 for 才能接人。

phrases.note: listen 是「注意聽」的動作，接受詞時要加 to；hear 是「聽見」，不加 to。
examples: I listen to music on the bus.
我在公車上聽音樂。
Listen to your teacher carefully.
仔細聽老師說。

questions.stem: 聽（注意聽）
questions.why: listen to＝聽。
listen 後面接受詞要加 to。

questions.answer: They are listening to music in the living room
questions.why: listen to + 聽的東西。

phrases.note: put on 是「穿上」這個動作；wear 是「穿著」的狀態。相反是 take off。
examples: Put on your coat; it is cold outside.
把外套穿上，外面很冷。
He put on his glasses and read the letter.
他戴上眼鏡，讀了那封信。

questions.stem: 穿上；戴上
questions.why: put on＝穿上、戴上。

questions.stem: It is raining. ___ your raincoat before you go out.
questions.why: 下雨要穿上雨衣。

questions.answer: She put on her hat and went out
questions.why: put on 的過去式同形，後面接穿戴的東西。

phrases.note: 表示「最少、起碼」，也可以用來安慰別人（至少……還好）。
examples: You should sleep at least seven hours.
你至少要睡七小時。
We lost the game, but at least we tried.
我們輸了，但至少我們試過了。

questions.stem: 至少
questions.why: at least＝至少；at last＝最後、終於。

questions.stem: The trip takes ___ four hours by bus, maybe longer.
questions.why: 「最少四小時，可能更久」用 at least。

questions.zh: 你每天至少應該喝八杯水。
questions.answer: You should drink at least eight glasses of water every day
questions.why: at least 放在數量前面。

phrases.note: 回答別人的請求或問題時表示「當然可以、當然是」。
examples: "Can you help me?" "Of course!"
「你可以幫我嗎？」「當然！」
Of course she was tired after the race.
她比賽後當然會累。

questions.stem: 當然
questions.why: of course＝當然。

questions.stem: "May I borrow your eraser?" "___ . Here you are."
questions.why: 答應別人的請求用 Of course。

questions.zh: 當然，我明天會去參加你的生日派對。
questions.answer: Of course I will go to your birthday party tomorrow
questions.why: Of course 放句首表示「當然」。
